svg.aria-label: Seventh-prefix triangle-removal probability against Pasch count for the 80 classes of cyclic Steiner triple systems on 31 points
svg.text: How random triangle removal sees a Steiner system (31 points)
Delete random triangles from K₃₁. The chance the first seven all lie in a given triple system T is set by its Pasch count.
Pasch: four triangles on six points
abc, ade, fbd, fce: any two share one point
plus a constant; nothing else enters q₇.
80 classes of cyclic STS(31), one dot each (dot area ∝ number of systems)
Pasch count of T (axis broken between 372 and 1085)
Pasch-free: every one beats every system with a Pasch
grey numbers: systems in that column
excess over the lowest, units of 10−28
why the Pasch count decides, for every STS(31): change in q₇ per unit, same linear scale
all other patterns, worst case combined
so fewer Pasch always wins (theorem, order 31): even the worst case leaves a margin of 2.70 × 10−25
Data: Lattice's exact census of the 2048 cyclic systems (80 classes); theorem covers all STS(31). Seven-step prefix only; equal Pasch counts not ranked.
